Subject: Post-demo alignment and quick next steps

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Really appreciated the walkthrough of your use cases for the customer support corpus and the mixed structured/unstructured data (ticket text + policy docs). Quick recap and a concrete proposal so we can keep momentum: 

What I heard as the primary asks:
- High relevance for short answer extraction + safe grounding to policy text
- Low hallucination tolerance (legal + compliance impact)
- Budget sensitivity on token spend for the 100k monthly query footprint

Recommended immediate next steps (proposed 2-week discovery sprint):
1) Baseline bench: run our rw-emb-2k (512-d) + rw-llm-3b baseline for throughput/latency and basic QA accuracy on your sample set (we can do this within hosted Redwood API).
2) Retrieval sweep: compare sparse (BM25) + dense (faiss, RW embeddings) hybrid vs dense-only. We recommend candidate_pool_top_k = 100, chunk size 500–800 chars for policy docs.
3) Reranker A/B: try a lightweight cross-encoder "rw-rerank-cross-enc-small" for top-20 candidates vs a pairwise light reranker for 50 candidates to balance latency/cost.
4) Prompt & eval set: you provide 400 queries from production; we'll return an initial results CSV and a small prompt set (attached stub) for sanity checks.

Attachments: helix_sample_prompts.csv (sample prompt set), retrieval_benchmarks_q1.csv (baseline template).

Two small asks from our side:
- Can you share a 400-query sample (PII-free) or let us instrument a read-only export?
- Please loop in Carlos (ML lead) on the technical sync — we want their timing for a deep-dive on data slicing.

If this looks good I'll schedule a 60-min technical kickoff with Karthik (SE) and Marissa (Solutions) next week; proposed windows: Tue/Wed 9–11am PT.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Samantha —

Great questions. See inline and a short technical note below. We'll add these to the kickoff agenda.

On Mon, Mar 15, 2027 at 9:18 AM Samantha Liu <samantha@helix-analytics.com> wrote:
> 1) Reranker latency: our SLA target for interactive support is sub-500ms end-to-end. Can you share expected latency ranges for the two reranker options you mentioned (small cross-encoder vs pairwise)? What CPU/GPU assumptions?

- Short answer: on a dedicated GPU (A10G/NVIDIA T4 class) we expect
  * rw-rerank-cross-enc-small (top-20 rerank): ~80–180ms median per request for the reranker stage (batching dependent), overall E2E for LLM + retrieval + rerank ~250–450ms depending on prompt length and streaming usage.
  * pairwise-light (top-50 candidates): ~150–350ms median for reranker stage but can reduce model footprint if you run it on CPU-optimized nodes with optimized kernels; tradeoff is higher candidate recall at cost of latency/cost.

Assumptions: 1–3 request batch size at inference time; retrieval vector lookup is ~10–25ms; LLM generation latency varies by model choice (rw-llm-3b ~60–140ms per 128 tokens on our hosted runtime). We'll include a latency profile matrix in the kickoff pack.

> 2) Grounding metrics: what exact metrics will you compute in the bench?

- We'll compute: Grounding Precision@K (fraction of answers with at least one supporting doc in top-K), Hallucination Rate (manual label + heuristic flags), Passage Recall@K, and Answer Factuality score (human-rated 1–5 sample). We will also surface per-query confidence and link each answer to the supporting doc id/offset so you can audit.

> 3) Prompt set: happy to share 400 queries but want to confirm you prefer anonymized CSV (we'll remove PII). Also are you able to accept an encrypted S3 upload?

- Anonymized CSV is perfect. We can accept an encrypted S3 upload (we'll provide a presigned URL) or you can drop into the secure folder in our Drive link. Will share the presigned S3 details after you confirm.

Proposed agenda for Tue 16 Mar 10–11am PT:
- intros + goals (10m)
- data / prompt set review + upload method (10m)
- retrieval sweep plan & metric definitions (15m)
- reranker options + latency/cost tradeoffs (15m)
- logistics: roles, deliverables, timeline (10m)

I've attached the sample prompt CSV again and a baseline benchmark template so Carlos can preview.

—Grace

Hi Samantha / Grace —

Thanks — I'll join the kickoff and bring a concise technical plan. A few quick implementation notes we plan to bring to the meeting so you can prep:

1) Embeddings: we'll use rw-emb-2k with 1k–2k vector dim option (default 1536 for your dataset). We'll publish the sample embedding recall curve in the kickoff doc.
2) Chunking & indexing: suggest 500–750 char chunks with sliding overlap 128 chars; index with Faiss IVFPQ for dense + a BM25 index for text-first recall.
3) Candidate selection & rerank: pipeline = dense + sparse hybrid -> top_k_candidates=100 -> rerank top_n=20 for cross-encoder option. Expect initial run cost ~ $0.02/query in hosted baseline (we'll provide exact cost sims).
4) Eval artifacts we'll deliver by EOD Week 1: CSV with per-query top-K ids, reranker scores, grounding flags, and a short report with precision/recall tables.

I've uploaded a one-page evaluation plan and the sample prompt set to the Drive link Grace shared; bringing the link into the meeting stream. Looking forward to the sync — see you at 10:00 PT.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
